selectedSources.title: Garifuna: The Voice of the Ancestors — 2013 festival profile
selectedSources.publisher: Smithsonian Center for Folklife and Cultural Heritage / Smithsonian Latino Center
selectedSources.annotation: A dated festival introduction connects Saint Vincent/Yurumein, British exile in 1797 and Central American/U.S. communities. Participant perspectives place language, teaching and public performance in intergenerational context.
selectedSources.contentReviewScope: Actual 2013 programme body: Flavio Alvarez statement, main historical/diaspora introduction, James Lovell caption and participant roles. Normal HTTP 200 full HTML retrieved and selected text inspected after web-reader timeout.
selectedSources.accessNotes: Selected HTML body only, not all festival material, linked recordings, histories underlying its synthesis or pictured participants. No current population distribution/count, universal ancestry test or present officeholder claim. Images not reproduced from this source.
selectedSources.sourcePerspective: Smithsonian Center for Folklife and Cultural Heritage / Smithsonian Latino Center publication; named participant/project perspectives are attributed. No universal community endorsement.

selectedSources.title: Garifuna — language structure and community documentation projects
selectedSources.annotation: A language-documentation organization describes Arawakan affiliation, contact vocabulary, New York community settings and collaborations using songs to teach language. Its accounts of programmes are organizational descriptions rather than independent impact evaluations.
selectedSources.contentReviewScope: Actual page Affiliation paragraph; selected Morphosyntax introduction; ELA’s Work paragraphs describing documentation with James Lovell and Daniel Kaufman; In New York community-setting paragraphs; Nursery Rhymes project introduction and Yugacure project description. Actual web-reader body inspected; not all example paradigms or embedded media.
selectedSources.accessNotes: Undated webpage: no current speaker totals, percentage distributions, success/outcome claims or language-only identity rule adopted. Shipwreck-origin narrative, gendered-register origin hypotheses and exclusivity claims are not used. Embedded recordings, underlying cited books, grant records and all12songs not watched/read. No reproduction of lyrics, ceremonial text or media.
selectedSources.sourcePerspective: Endangered Language Alliance publication; named participant/project perspectives are attributed. No universal community endorsement.
